title: Vacuum Relief Valve

introduction.definition: A vacuum relief valve (vacuum breaker) admits air into a tank or vessel when its internal pressure falls below a set vacuum, preventing implosion. Vacuum is created when a tank is pumped out, when hot vapours condense or when weather cools a tank. When the set point is reached, atmospheric pressure pushes the pallet open against its spring or weight; air flows in until pressures balance.
key_points: Set vacuum must be below the tank's vacuum design rating
Sized for maximum pump-out + thermal in-breathing (API 2000)
introduction.summary: A vacuum relief valve protects a tank or vessel from collapsing under vacuum — for example when it is emptied quickly or when hot vapour condenses. When the internal pressure falls below the set vacuum, atmospheric pressure pushes the pallet open against its spring and air flows in; when the pressures equalise the spring closes it.

foundation: Support the valve and adjoining pipe so the body does not carry pipe weight or thermal loads; heavy valves need their own supports.
alignment: Align flanges face-to-face and bore-to-bore before bolting; never pull pipes into place with the bolts.
Respect the flow-direction arrow on the body.
piping: Mount vertically on a roof nozzle at least as large as the valve inlet.
Keep the inlet free from frost and product build-up; heat-trace if needed.
commissioning: Check the valve strokes fully and smoothly.
Pressure-test the line (shell test) with the valve partly open; do not use the valve to blind a test above its seat rating.
Record the as-installed position and set points.

causes: Blocked screen, stuck pallet, undersized valve

video_tutorials.title: Vacuum Relief Valve — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Vacuum Relief Valve.
A vacuum relief valve (vacuum breaker) admits air into a tank or vessel when its internal pressure falls below a set vacuum, preventing implosion.
Vacuum is created when a tank is pumped out, when hot vapours condense or when weather cools a tank.
When the set point is reached, atmospheric pressure pushes the pallet open against its spring or weight; air flows in until pressures balance.
Typical applications include atmospheric and low-pressure storage tanks; evaporators, condensers and steam-heated vessels; pipelines at high points (vacuum breakers); tank trucks and IBCs.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Valve Body & Seat Ring, Weather Hood & Bird Screen.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Vacuum Relief Valve — Operation

script.narration: How the Vacuum Relief Valve works.
Normally the spring holds the pallet against the seat — the tank is sealed.
As the tank is emptied, internal pressure drops below atmospheric.
At the set vacuum, atmospheric pressure pushes the pallet inward against the spring.
Air enters through the hood and screen into the tank.
When pressure equalises the spring recloses the pallet.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Vacuum Relief Valve — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Vacuum Relief Valve.
Inspect screen and hood for blockage, ice or nests.
Lift-test the pallet and check seat.
Replace pallet seal and spring.
Watch for tank collapse: buckled roof/shell. Common cause: blocked screen, stuck pallet, undersized valve.
Watch for leakage / emissions: vapour release. Common cause: damaged seat.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
